maml:description.maml:para: Creates an experimental, runspace-owned AppInstall context without activating the native manager.

Returns a caller-owned IDisposable context. Creation performs no search, installation, native activation, account lookup, or settings operation. Dispose the context in finally. It is also disposed when its owning runspace closes. Later operations must reuse this explicit context in the same runspace; it cannot be used from another runspace or remoting session. Removing the module does not dispose caller-owned contexts.

Windows 10 build 19041 or later and PowerShell 7.4 or later are required. Microsoft documents AppInstallManager access as protected by a private capability restricted to Microsoft-developed apps. Observed runtime access is not an official third-party support guarantee. Creating a context does not check or grant native authorization.

maml:alert.maml:para: Get-AppInstallItem and Get-AppInstallSettings read caller-scoped inventory and approved settings through this explicit context. Request-AppInstallUpdateSearch is a separately confirmed caller-scoped paused-queue mutation. No settings mutation, control, entitlement, or ForUser command is provided.

maml:description.maml:para: Reads immutable caller-scoped AppInstall queue and current-status snapshots.

Requires an explicit context from New-AppInstallContext in the same runspace. The first read lazily activates the native manager. This command reads AppInstallItems, or AppInstallItemsWithGroupSupport and Children when IncludeChildren is set. It never searches for updates, submits requests, changes settings, or invokes controls or ForUser APIs.

ProductId and PackageFamilyName use exact ordinal case-insensitive matching, not wildcards. Values within each filter are alternatives; both filters must match when both are supplied. Filters apply after a complete capture. A matched parent includes its complete subtree; a matching descendant of an unmatched parent is emitted with its ParentLocalItemId. Matching descendants are not emitted again beneath a matching ancestor.

Failed reads, disappearing items, conflicting parents, cycles, or inventory limits produce errors and no results for that capture. Unsupported optional members are explicitly Unavailable, never silent false or zero values. Installation errors returned by the status ErrorCode property remain data. A returned item, percentage, IsStaged or ReadyForLaunch is not proof of installation completion.

Local IDs are correlation for projected item identities retained in the last successful capture, not native IDs or control authorization. Removed identities are pruned on a successful scan and all retained references are released when the context is disposed. Captures are bounded to 4096 distinct items and 128 group levels; exceeding a limit errors rather than truncates. Caller scope does not identify an account, SID, or the owner of every visible queue item.

Microsoft documents AppInstallManager access as protected by a private capability restricted to Microsoft-developed apps. Observed runtime access is not an official third-party support guarantee. Nonempty item/status/group paths have deterministic fake-adapter coverage, not a claim of live support in every host.
The live, caller-owned context from the same runspace. Dispose it explicitly when finished.
One or more exact product IDs. Ambiguous native names can match multiple distinct local identities; no control target is inferred.
One or more exact package family names, combined with the product filter when supplied.
Read the grouped collection and child relationships. Without this switch children are Unknown rather than assumed absent.

dev:remarks.maml:para: Access is subject to the native private-capability restriction. No updates are searched for or queued.

maml:description.maml:para: Reads selected experimental AppInstallManager settings through an explicit caller-owned context.

Requires an explicit AppInstallContext created in the current runspace. Reuses its single lazy manager; never creates a hidden context or process-global manager. Creation of the context does not activate native code. This reader activates it only after the selected member passes availability checks. Dispose the context in finally; module removal does not dispose it. These getters are synchronous, sequential observations, not an atomic device-settings snapshot.

By default only AutoUpdateSetting and CanInstallForAllUsers are read. AcquisitionIdentity is not read by default. Select it explicitly with -Property AcquisitionIdentity; -Property replaces the default selection and accepts only the three exact names, not numeric aliases, wildcards or All. Repeated names are read once. An unselected identity remains null and Unknown, without even a metadata probe for that property. Nothing logs an identity value to verbose, debug or information output.

AcquisitionIdentity is an observation of the supplied manager context, not a verified account/SID or evidence of persistence across managers. AutoUpdateSetting is the documented device setting, not an isolated per-context or per-user preference. Independent contexts do not isolate device-wide policy. Its integer value preserves the native enum, including future codes: Disabled = 0, Enabled = 1, DisabledByPolicy = 2, EnabledByPolicy = 3. CanInstallForAllUsers is a read-only calling-process privilege observation, not a privilege grant, private-capability check, or guarantee that installation is available or will succeed.

The immutable snapshot includes ContextId (local correlation, not a SID or native install ID), Caller user scope, per-property scope, RequestedProperties and ReadProperties. Unselected values are Unknown. Missing types or members are Unavailable and are not invoked. Available false, zero and an explicitly requested empty identity are retained as observed values. Operational errors terminate without a partial snapshot. ErrorRecord retains the original exception, HRESULT and typed phase metadata; the default error message does not render raw native diagnostics, which can contain sensitive data.

Windows 10 build 19041 or later and PowerShell 7.4 or later are required; every selected member is checked before each read. Microsoft documents AppInstallManager access as protected by a private capability restricted to Microsoft-developed apps. Observed getter access is not an official third-party support guarantee. Administrator access, runFullTrust, successful activation and CanInstallForAllUsers are not substitutes for that restriction. No settings writes, identity changes, ForUser, installation, entitlement, search or queue-control actions are performed.

An explicit, live AppInstallContext owned by the current runspace. Reuse it across reads and dispose it in finally. A detached JSON object, another runspace's context or a disposed context cannot be used.

The exact properties to read: AcquisitionIdentity, AutoUpdateSetting and CanInstallForAllUsers. Defaults to AutoUpdateSetting and CanInstallForAllUsers. An explicit list replaces these defaults. AcquisitionIdentity is sensitive and is read only when explicitly selected; no All or wildcard selector is accepted.

dev:remarks.maml:para: Reads only the device auto-update setting and calling-process privilege observation. Does not change either value.
Reads only acquisition identity. Treat the returned value as sensitive; no account/SID mapping or persistent-user-setting semantics are inferred.

maml:description.maml:para: Requests an experimental caller-scoped all-app update search that can queue discovered updates paused.

This is a queue mutation, not a read-only search. Uses only SearchForAllUpdatesAsync(correlationVector, clientId, AppUpdateOptions). AutomaticallyDownloadAndInstallUpdateIfFound and AllowForcedAppRestart are both explicitly fixed false before submission. False still adds discovered updates to the install queue in a paused state; no automatic download/install or forced restart is requested. ShouldProcess protects the call with high-impact confirmation. WhatIf and declined confirmation emit nothing and perform no native activation, metadata probe, options construction or search.

Requires an explicit live context owned by the current runspace, plus caller-supplied nonempty, non-whitespace CorrelationVector and ClientId strings. They are forwarded unchanged with no generated or hardcoded client identity, account lookup, acquisition identity write or catalog override. No per-app, ForUser, alternate overload or broader-scope fallback is available. Dispose the context in finally; this command never disposes caller-owned contexts.

Emits one immutable AppInstallRequestSnapshot only after the native search operation, operation cleanup and item capture succeed, including a successful empty search. Acceptance=Accepted means an async handle was returned. OperationState=Completed is search completion, not installation completion. ItemsAvailability=Available with zero items is an observed empty result, not a failure or proof that no updates exist in other scopes. Returned items retain their own status and child availability; paused, staged or launch-ready items do not imply installation success.

RequestId is local per-request correlation, not a native install ID. ContextId, local item/parent IDs, product/family identities, Caller scope and the supplied native correlation strings are preserved. Search capture merges a bounded identity cache without pruning unrelated inventory identities; exceeding 4096 retained items fails instead of evicting or truncating. The next successful inventory scan retains its normal pruning behavior. Serialized snapshots are detached observations, not native handles or control authorization.

The default request view shows local IDs, API/scope/outcome fields and item count; it omits CorrelationVector, ClientId, item payloads and raw errors. The raw public properties and JSON are unchanged, and explicit inspection such as Format-List * displays their values. Default formatting is not redaction, secret storage or a security boundary.

Failures terminate without a success result or partial item list. ErrorRecord.TargetObject contains the typed request with original error/HRESULT and failure phase, including cleanup errors. A submission that throws has Unknown acceptance, not proof of rejection or rollback. Stopping the pipeline stops only local waiting and releases the async adapter; it never calls native Cancel or changes queued items. A stopped pipeline can suppress output and errors, so missing output is not evidence that submission did not occur. No hard timeout can forcibly interrupt a synchronous native call.

Windows 10 build 19041 or later and PowerShell 7.4 or later are required; required types, the three-argument method and writable safety properties are preflighted before activation. Microsoft documents AppInstallManager access as protected by a private capability restricted to Microsoft-developed apps. Observed runtime access is not an official third-party support guarantee. Administrator access and runFullTrust alone do not grant that capability. Nonempty/grouped results are covered by deterministic fakes, not new live support evidence.
An explicit live AppInstallContext created in this runspace. No hidden context is created. Dispose it in finally.

The caller-provided correlation vector passed unchanged to the documented overload. No default or account-derived value is generated. Retained in the request; treat correlation data as potentially sensitive.

The caller's client identifier passed unchanged to the documented overload. No fabricated identity or authorization is supplied by the module. Retained in the request but omitted from confirmation messages.
Preview the queue mutation without any native API call or success output.
Confirm the caller-scoped all-app search and paused-queue side effect. Declining invokes no native API.
